newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shareholders to vote on Elbit split.
newsitem.headline: Shareholders to vote on Elbit split.

text.p: Israel's Elbit Ltd said on Tuesday it would hold a general shareholders' meeting on November 6 to approve splitting the company into three separate companies.

Shareholders will be asked to vote on a proposal to create two new companies, Elbit Medical Imaging (EMI), which would take over Elbit's medical-imaging activities, and Elbit Systems Ltd (ESL), which would incorporate Elbit's defence-electronics business.
Elbit would continue the civilian activity, including telecommunications, video products and industrial control systems, the company said in a statement to the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.
In the framework of the split, shareholders would receive one share each in ESL and EMI for each share they hold in Elbit.

Shares of the two new companies will be traded both on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange and on Nasdaq. Before the share issue, both ESL and EMI will publish prospectuses in Israel and registration statements in the United States.

Medical-imaging operations account for 53 percent of Elbit's assets, defence for 18 percent and civilian operations for 29 percent. Elbit will transfer assets worth an estimated 590 million shekels to the two new companies.
Elbit is 37 percent owned by Elron Electronic Industries Ltd. It is also traded on Nasdaq.

In the first six months of the year Elbit sales reached $431 million against $469 million in the same period last year. Net profit was $5 million against $11 million in the first six months of last year.
